concerns.concern: Package-level dependency cycle (SCC#1, size=6) binds packages/quay/src to its own subsystems — src/cli, src/fan-in, src/gate, src/gate/config, src/gate/factories. The top-level core module and the gate/fan-in layers form a mutually-recursive boundary, so the intended layer split (core vs gate vs fan-in) is not one-directional; ownership between the core source root and the gate subsystem is entangled rather than a clean dependency edge.
concerns.what_to_investigate: Identify which concrete edges close the SCC (at least one edge from each layer back into packages/quay/src) and whether any can be moved to a lower-level module — noting that a kernel seam (packages/quay/src/kernel) already exists and is imported by plugin/scripts, which is evidence a clean low-level seam is an established pattern here.

concerns.concern: No single owner resolves a task's landing baseline. The default landing literal "develop" is duplicated (~20 sites / 17 files), and SPEC-goal-branch §4.3 explicitly requires one shared resolver (mergeTarget = goal/<id> when the goal is active + branch:true, else develop) used simultaneously by three call sites: worktree --base, fan-in mergeTarget, and fan-in lock selection — with the spec warning that a mismatch makes fork-point and landing point diverge. Landing-baseline ownership is currently implicit and duplicated rather than canonicalized, and the goal-branch feature (drilled on GOAL-905) depends on fixing exactly this.
concerns.what_to_investigate: Enumerate the real call sites of the "develop" default (the spec's 20/17 count is explicitly an upper bound, not all requiring change) and confirm whether any single resolveTaskMergeTarget exists today or must be introduced; also check whether the plugin layer that spawns fan-in is the right owner given its existing dependency footprint on packages/quay/src.

concerns.concern: Task status writes have no single owner. One raw helper, plugin/scripts/task-ops.ts:patchStatusField, rewrites the `status:` line with no transition check (only an optional fromStatus compare-and-swap). It is called directly from three modules, each holding its own transition rules: driver-filters.ts (2 sites, including needs-human), ready-pool-check.ts (2 sites, todo↔ready) and worker-fan-in.ts (4 sites, done/ready reset). The Core lifecycle table (gate/lifecycle.ts TRANSITIONS) is not on any of these paths. The archived history replay shows 17.7% of real flips fall outside that table, because the table lacks the needs-human and superseded edges. So the 'canonical' transition table and the actual writers have drifted apart. The goal-branch spec adds a second dimension: `done` will mean 'landed on mergeTarget', with status written to two places (B2). That raises the cost of having no single status-transition owner.
concerns.what_to_investigate: This is decision-ready in shape: first add the missing needs-human/superseded edges (the readings name that as the prerequisite), then send all 8 call sites through one transition-checked writer. One thing to confirm before slicing: whether any of the 3 caller modules already consults TRANSITIONS before calling patchStatusField. The dossier excerpts don't show it either way.

concerns.concern: There is a package-level dependency cycle inside Core. One strongly connected component of size 6 spans packages/quay/src, cli, fan-in, gate, gate/config and gate/factories. The root package, the CLI layer and the gate engine/fan-in subsystems all depend on each other, so there is no layering direction among them. This is a dependency-boundary and ownership problem: it is unclear whether gate or fan-in owns its config/factories, or the root does.
concerns.what_to_investigate: List the file-level edges that close the cycle, especially any edge from gate/* or fan-in back to the src root or cli. Find the smallest cut set that breaks it. The dossier only shows which packages are in the cycle, not which edges form it.

concerns.concern: The boundary between plugin/scripts and Core is unclear. plugin/scripts has 86 dependency edges into packages/quay (65 to the src root, 17 to src/kernel, 2 each to gate and fan-in). Yet the archived readings justify keeping duplicate Task parsers (task-parsing.ts ↔ task-schema.ts) on the grounds that the plugin 'cannot static import' packages/. Either the plugin can depend on Core, so the duplicate parsers are unnecessary copies, or it can't, so these 86 edges rely on a bundling step that isn't stated in the evidence. The kernel subset (proc-identity, task-shape-artifacts, env-merge) looks like a deliberate shared kernel. The 65 edges to the src root don't.
concerns.what_to_investigate: Find out how the plugin build resolves imports from packages/quay/src (inlined by the bundler, or failing at runtime). Classify the 65 src-root edges: are they kernel-shaped utilities, or reaches into Core internals? The answer decides whether the parser duplication is necessary or just leftover drift.

response.negative_control: Three independent controls, each separating 'worked' from 'looks like it worked'. (1) Edge-table falsity: feed the decision layer a genuinely undeclared pair vs a declared-but-illegal pair (`isDeclaredIllegalPair`) and assert TWO DIFFERENT values, not a single 'not-allowed' — otherwise an absent/empty table is indistinguishable from a passing check (hard rule 3b). harnessability.constraints: Scope limited to the promote/retreat edges; fan-in and needs-human/branch-sync writers untouched; ONE decision function (not two parallel paths) so the record and the patch come from the same call and a bypass is detectable as a record/flip mismatch; the record goes to an existing carrier, not a new log.

(2) The record is emitted only from a fixture/injected seam — the production-carrier AC goes red (hard rule 4 推论三). (3) The decision layer collapses 'undeclared' into 'illegal' — the two-value negative control fails (hard rule 3b). The two transitions are exactly the two writers T1 puts in scope; the table the decision layer must consult already exists with zero non-definition callers, so the layer is wiring, not invention; and the record reuses an existing gate-event carrier rather than a new log. (D) Web reuse identity: a test that drives `handleDriverLifecycle` must hit the same `runDriver` export that the CLI uses, by comparing module identity or realpath.
response.abandon_or_reconsider_condition: Reconsider, falling back to S1-alt or re-scoping, if the move would drag more than the listed pieces: for example, if `runDriver`'s transitive closure reaches cli-only modules (`cli/shared.ts`, `cli/flags.ts`, `cli/help.ts`) whose relocation would itself be a second ownership decision. That would contradict findings:T1 #5's claim that these are layer-neutral primitives. Abandon or re-investigate if: (1) the before reading does not reproduce SCC=6 with the cycle matrix as stated; (2) the after reading is anything other than 4 with the exact member set above, which means hidden edges (for example the 3 unattributed cli inbound relations in package-metrics turn out to come from in-cycle code); (3) the move needs new `layers.yml` edges or a kernel placement; (4) `quay --help` latency regresses because the vocabulary module picked up imports; (5) the parity check can only be kept green by weakening its entries. Also stop if the slice starts to touch gate/* or fan-in/* source to make the numbers work. Per the methodology, the metric serves the scope.

harnessability.inputs: Fork-point commit, which is the develop tip at activation (cutoff 1025ab9512de as reference). The ArchGuard 0.1.38 TypeScript scope. The two root import sites and the three cli importers. The parity-check entries.
harnessability.outputs: A goal branch with one or a few serial tasks: the vocabulary move plus the dead-import drop, then the driver-control move. Evidence JSON with the before/after SCC member list and size, root→cli relation count, definition-site counts, the (A)–(D) negative-control readings, and `quay --help` timing.
harnessability.constraints: Branch:true goal, private worktree off develop. `runDriver` signatures, result shape and vocabulary values stay byte-identical. The vocabulary module stays zero-import. Root never imports through cli. No production restarts. Self-host identity: in the worktree, the resolved realpaths of the new root modules must fall inside the goal worktree.
harnessability.acceptance: Three-state exit (0 achieved / 1 with same-line CAUSE= / 3 not evaluated). AC-a: structure is done when `git grep` of root importing `./cli/` = 0, the definition-site counts are 1 at root, and parity, typecheck and scoped tests are green. AC-b: ArchGuard before shows SCC=6 and after shows SCC=4 with the exact member set, and negative controls A–D behave as specified. AC-c: merge shape is exactly 1 first-parent merge commit on develop, and the post-merge ArchGuard reading on develop still gives 4.
harnessability.failure_mode: The bad case is a quiet pass: SCC drops to 5 while a reviewer accepts "it went down". Or root keeps a re-export path through cli that ArchGuard misattributes. Or the parity check silently stops covering the vocabulary after the file path changes. Controls A, B and C exist to make each of these red rather than looking like success.

response.minimum_sufficiency_rationale: Sufficient: with both root→cli relations removed, the cycle matrix leaves cli with zero inbound edges from SCC members, so cli must leave. fan-in's only in-cycle inbound edge comes from cli, so it leaves too. That is a guaranteed 2-member reduction from 2 import sites. Minimum: either edge alone leaves the cycle intact, so the pair cannot be split. The cli→root direction (62) is legitimate and stays. The remaining gate/root core is a separate, larger question. No new abstraction is introduced, only relocation to the layer both consumers can reach, following the GOAL-032 thin-move precedent. The dead `HOSTED_SERVICE_NAMES` import is removed only because it is on a line this slice already rewrites. propose-goal over investigate: T1 already established the edge count, the symbols, the consumers, and that no other member feeds cli. The one open premise, `runDriver`'s closure, is a cheap precondition check inside the first task and a defined abandon trigger, not a question that needs its own investigation round.
